name: screenshots
//: No target here captures: the capture is `just screenshots`, which is no Nx target at all, and that is what keeps it out of `just check`, `just gate` and CI's check job. What this project holds is the curated fixture, the vendored renderer font and the durable note — a project like everything else, so a change to one is selected by the graph rather than escaping it. It depends on no other project, and the only edge is the one `workspace` has to every project. screenshots/AGENTS.md is why.

bootstrap.//: Nothing to provision, deliberately: the pinned renderer is installed on demand by `just screenshots-tools`, and putting a screenshot tool on the gate's provisioning path would make an informational tier a prerequisite of the gate.

format.//: Uncached: it rewrites the tree in place. Only this project's own JSON is formatted — biome has no formatter for Markdown front matter, a TrueType font or an SVG.

lint.//: The static half: it reconciles every version this capture restates, the scene inventory against the committed baseline, and every image the README embeds against what is committed. It takes no screenshot and needs neither screencomp nor the renderer, so it runs in CI's check job like every other lint. The workspaceRoot inputs SELECT this project as well as hash it, which is the point: a README that drops an image, or a workflow whose two screencomp pins part, has to re-run this. llmlint: ignore-file[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] JSON has no comment to scope a directive to those inputs, which is what this is about: Nx selects a PROJECT rather than a target, so they select `test` too — and there is no expensive tier behind that edge, both checks cloning with `git clone --shared` and the whole target finishing in under two seconds (measured). Dropping the inputs instead would stop the reconciliation re-running when a README image is deleted, which is the defect it exists to catch.

typecheck.//: Declared and empty. Target names are uniform because `nx affected` fans out by name, and there is nothing here between reading a file and running it: the capture machinery is shell, whose static analysis is the bash 3.2 scan under `scripts:lint`, and the fixture is data the real binary parses in the `test` target's own scenes.

test.//: Uncached and serial, and both for the same reason the workspace project's own test target is: each of the two clones this repository into a scratch tree, which no input glob in this tree describes. The first drives the real pre-push guard and the real hook through every outcome each owes, with screencomp and the capture stubbed at the subprocess seam scripts/check-pre-push-provisioning.sh stubs `just` at. The second drives the renderer resolver and the baseline writer against a stand-in tool location and a stand-in installer, as scripts/check-scoped-release-plz.sh does for the other scoped tool: no network, and nothing installed on the host is read or touched.

coverage.//: Declared and empty. The 95% line floor is measured by instrumenting a compiled crate or an interpreted SDK; there is no line coverage for a shell script or a Markdown fixture, and what stands in its place is the guard check above driving the real guard until it refuses.
